name: theme-popover-from-a-space-dot
description:
The Theme Studio as a movable child window off a space dot. Right-click the dot for the active space, pick Change Theme, and the /theme route opens in its own widget above the sidebar and the page. The studio evals target /theme; the menu evals still target /sidebar.

WHY THE MENU AND THE PICK GO THROUGH eval RATHER THAN cgevent: the dots sit at the bottom of a 280px strip, so a screen coordinate for one is a number this scenario has never measured and would silently retarget the moment a row height changes. The contextmenu event is dispatched on the dot itself and travels through installRowMenu's real listener, so the branch under test is the product's, and the item is found by its own label rather than by a position in the menu.

THE EDIT IS THE OPACITY SLIDER at 0.92 - a step multiple, distinct from the fixture's 0.3, and not an integer, so file_value.py's type check cannot be satisfied by an int/float coincidence. 'Atrium: theme preview applied' is BrowserController::PreviewSpaceTheme's own line, so the preview reaching the window behind is read from the browser rather than inferred from a repaint.

PERSISTENCE IS ASSERTED TWICE, because the two answers are different: file_contains on themes.json says the bytes were written, and reopening the popover says the core hands the saved value back to the studio. The fixture stages 0.3 there, so neither can pass against a build that wrote nothing - file_value.py refuses an expected value the staged copy already held.

THE 'after' CAPTURE IS TAKEN WITH THE POPOVER CLOSED, so the theme_changed region compares the window's own backdrop rather than a card sitting on top of it. THE 'before-drag' AND 'popover' CAPTURES ARE THE TWO FRAMES THAT SHOW THE STUDIO OPEN, before and after the header drag.

actions.note: gate: the startup tab committed, so the app and the fixture are live
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
the window's own backdrop, the fixture's opacity-0.3 gradient, before any studio edit

actions.expression: (() => { const dot = [...document.querySelectorAll('.sdot')].find((d) => d.dataset.spaceIndex === '0'); if (!dot) return 'no-dot'; const r = dot.getBoundingClientRect(); dot.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('contextmenu', {bubbles: true, clientX: r.left + 4, clientY: r.top + 4})); return [...document.querySelectorAll('.ctxitem')].map((b) => b.textContent).join(','); })()
actions.note: the dot's own context menu, opened through installRowMenu's real listener and read back by label

actions.expression: (() => { const item = [...document.querySelectorAll('.ctxitem')].find((b) => b.textContent === 'Change Theme'); if (!item) return 'no-item'; item.click(); return 'clicked'; })()

actions.pattern: Atrium: theme studio popover opened for space 0
actions.note: the C++ half resolved the rail index to a space id and pushed the payload back

actions.expression: (() => { const body = document.querySelector('.tw-body'); if (!body) return 'no-body'; const name = document.querySelector('.tw-name'); return 'sliders=' + body.querySelectorAll('input[type="range"]').length + ' canvas=' + !!body.querySelector('canvas') + ' name=' + (name ? name.textContent : ''); })()
actions.note: the same six sliders and one gradient canvas theme-studio.js draws in the Spaces pane, this time inside the /theme window's own card. Counted inside .tw-body, not over the whole document: theme-picker.js appends its floating picker to document.body, so a document-wide count reads 7 and a second canvas
CDP evals never move macOS window ordering - reassert Atrium frontmost before the capture
the studio where PlaceThemeStudioAtAnchor put it, still over the sidebar column, before the header drag moves it

actions.expression: (() => { const head = document.querySelector('.tw-head'); if (!head) return 'no-head'; const init = (x, y) => ({bubbles: true, clientX: x, clientY: y, screenX: x, screenY: y, pointerId: 1, button: 0}); head.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerdown', init(100, 20))); head.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointermove', init(400, 140))); head.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerup', init(400, 140))); return 'dragged'; })()
actions.note: the header's own drag path: one pointerdown, one move of 300x120, one release - the widget should now sit over the page, not the sidebar. screenX/screenY are set because the header reads those, not clientX: a constructed PointerEvent leaves them at 0 and the delta would be 0
the drag went through chrome.send, so nothing raised the app - reassert it before the frame that has to show the moved card
the one frame showing the studio open and already dragged clear of the sidebar column

actions.expression: (() => { chrome.send('settingsThemeChanged', ['no-such-space', {name: 'Bogus', stops: [{x: 0.5, y: 0.5, color: '#00FF88', alpha: 1}], opacity: 1, effects: {grain: 0, vignette: 0, frost: 0, warmth: 0}, darkAdaptation: 0, version: 1}]); return 'sent'; })()
actions.note: the space id crosses from a renderer, so a bogus one has to be refused before it reaches atrium_core_set_space_theme - sent ahead of the real edit so the decline cannot be confused with it

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector('.theme-studio-slider[data-key="opacity"]'); if (!el) return 'no-slider'; el.value = '0.92'; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); return 'set:' + el.value; })()
actions.note: THE EDIT: a new value on the range input, then the same `input` event theme-studio.js listens for
BrowserController::PreviewSpaceTheme's own line - the edit reached a realised Atrium window

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.theme-studio-save'); if (!b) return 'no-save'; b.click(); return 'clicked'; })()

actions.note: the studio window's own save path, distinct from the settings window's 'Atrium: theme saved'

actions.expression: (() => { const dot = [...document.querySelectorAll('.sdot')].find((d) => d.dataset.spaceIndex === '0'); if (!dot) return 'no-dot'; const r = dot.getBoundingClientRect(); dot.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('contextmenu', {bubbles: true, clientX: r.left + 4, clientY: r.top + 4})); const item = [...document.querySelectorAll('.ctxitem')].find((b) => b.textContent === 'Change Theme'); if (!item) return 'no-item'; item.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
